content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To learn to fly, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Complete advanced cross-country navigation course (1 week)
Step 2. Study high-altitude aerodynamics (3 days)
Step 3. Attend meteorological theory seminars (4 days)
Step 4. Log night-flight hours with an instructor (10 hours)
Step 5. Final check-ride with FAA examiner (4 hours)
Step 6. Practice emergency engine-out procedures (5 hours)
Step 7. Research regional flight schools (2 days)
Step 8. Obtain FAA First-Class Medical Certificate (3 hours)
Step 9. Submit application for Private Pilot License (1 hour)
Step 10. Purchase pilot headset and flight bag (1 hour)
Step 11. Complete basic radio communication drills (2 hours)
Step 12. Review local airport taxiway diagrams (2 hours)
Step 13. Practice stall recovery techniques (3 hours)
Step 14. Perform a short-field takeoff and landing (1 hour)
Step 15. Pass the written aeronautical knowledge test (3 hours)
Step 16. Study federal aviation regulations (10 hours)
Step 17. Attend a pre-flight safety briefing (1 hour)
Step 18. Practice steep turns and maneuvers (2 hours)
Step 19. Conduct a supervised solo cross-country flight (5 hours)
Step 20. Watch instructional videos on cockpit instrumentation (6 hours)
Step 21. Memorize emergency checklists (4 hours)
Step 22. Practice landings in crosswind conditions (4 hours)
Step 23. Complete the primary ground school syllabus (40 hours)
Step 24. Perform weight and balance calculations (30 minutes)
Step 25. Calculate fuel requirements for a long trip (30 minutes)
Step 26. Practice touch-and-go landings (3 hours)
Step 27. Review the Pilot’s Operating Handbook (5 hours)
Step 28. Calibrate the onboard altimeter (15 minutes)
Step 29. Conduct the final solo flight (2 hours)
Step 30. Practice navigating via VOR stations (2 hours)
Step 31. Learn to interpret METAR weather reports (2 hours)
Step 32. Attend a seminar on cockpit resource management (6 hours)
Step 33. Practice recovery from unusual attitudes (2 hours)
Step 34. Complete a spin awareness training module (3 hours)
Step 35. Take a mock oral exam with a senior pilot (3 hours)
Step 36. Enroll in a flight training program (1 day)
Step 37. Perform a pre-flight inspection of the fuselage (30 minutes)
Step 38. Review the aircraft maintenance logs (1 hour)
Step 39. Visit the local Air Traffic Control tower (2 hours)
Step 40. Practice using the flight computer/E6B (2 hours)
Step 41. Buy a current sectional navigation chart (30 minutes)
Step 42. Learn to use the onboard GPS system (2 hours)
Step 43. Secure financing or a training budget (1 week)
Step 44. Meet with a certified flight instructor (2 hours)
Step 45. Practice soft-field landing techniques (2 hours)
Step 46. Apply for a student pilot certificate (1 hour)
Step 47. Clean the aircraft windscreen (15 minutes)
Step 48. Refuel the aircraft (20 minutes)
Step 49. Study the physics of lift and drag (5 hours)
Step 50. Verify the aircraft insurance coverage (1 hour)
Step 51. Learn to read NOTAMs (Notices to Air Missions) (1 hour)
Step 52. Secure the aircraft with tie-downs (15 minutes)
Step 53. Calculate the takeoff distance required (15 minutes)
Step 54. Practice radio calls at a towered airport (2 hours)
Step 55. Review the basic flight maneuvers manual (4 hours)
Step 56. Complete an introductory discovery flight (1 hour)
Step 57. Plan a flight route across three states (4 hours)
Step 58. Conduct a pre-flight engine run-up (15 minutes)
Step 59. Check the oil level and quality (10 minutes)
Step 60. Finalize the pilot logbook entries (30 minutes)
Step 61. Practice basic instrument flying under the hood (10 hours)
Step 62. Register for a student pilot account online (30 minutes)
Step 63. Inspect the landing gear and tires (15 minutes)
Step 64. Buy a pilot’s logbook (15 minutes)
Step 65. Watch a documentary on aviation history (2 hours)
Step 66. Discuss flight path with the instructor (30 minutes)
Step 67. Download a flight planning mobile app (10 minutes)
Step 68. Read "Stick and Rudder" by Wolfgang Langewiesche (12 hours)
Step 69. Practice slips to a landing (2 hours)
Step 70. Learn to use a transponder (30 minutes)
Step 71. Order a set of aviation headsets (15 minutes)
Step 72. Practice go-around procedures (1 hour)
Step 73. Subscribe to a digital flight weather service (15 minutes)
Step 74. Complete a cockpit orientation session (2 hours)
Step 75. Study the effects of density altitude (2 hours)
Step 76. Practice slow flight maneuvers (2 hours)
Step 77. Shadow a mechanic during a 100-hour inspection (8 hours)
Step 78. Learn to use a fuel sump tool (10 minutes)
Step 79. Interview several flight instructors (4 hours)
Step 80. Review the airport's noise abatement procedures (30 minutes)
Step 81. Practice using the mixture control (30 minutes)
Step 82. Execute a simulated engine failure on takeoff (1 hour)
Step 83. Analyze a surface analysis weather chart (1 hour)
Step 84. Learn to hand-propping an engine (safely) (1 hour)
Step 85. Set up a pilot profile in the FAA system (30 minutes)
Step 86. Get a set of cockpit checklists (15 minutes)
Step 87. Practice dead reckoning navigation (3 hours)
Step 88. Take a tour of the flight school hangar (1 hour)
Step 89. Buy a flight kneeboard (15 minutes)
Step 90. Study cloud formations and their meanings (3 hours)
Step 91. Put on a flight suit or comfortable clothes (5 minutes)
Step 92. Update the navigation database (30 minutes)
Step 93. Practice phonetic alphabet drills (1 hour)
Step 94. Check the density altitude at the runway (5 minutes)
Step 95. Perform a final cockpit "flow" check (10 minutes)
Step 96. Check the current weather briefing (20 minutes)
Step 97. Join a local flying club (1 hour)
Step 98. Confirm the runway is clear of debris (10 minutes)
Step 99. Adjust the pilot's seat and mirrors (5 minutes)
Step 100. Review the weight and balance for the day (15 minutes)
